mainTopic: הקדש בטעות in בית שמאי's view, רב חסדא on ox colors, and the בית הלל–בית שמאי debate over a mistaken consecration.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a quote from a later משנה about travelers who make נזיר vows about a stranger. בית שמאי say they are all נזירים even though some must be wrong. The גמרא answers that בית שמאי do hold a mistaken consecration (הקדש בטעות) counts, but the black-ox משנה rests on a different reason. אביי instead explains the black-ox case as a man speaking at noon about the past who got the facts wrong. The future-tense wording of the משנה is then read as past tense to fit his explanation. Next, רב חסדא's statements about which ox color is better are tested against the משנה. The idea that people consecrate 'with a stingy eye' holds once we know that in the גליל wine is worth more than oil. רב חסדא's view is limited to the קרמנאי breed. A new משנה then teaches what happens when a חכם upholds or dissolves a נזיר vow. That leads to a debate between בית הלל and בית שמאי over whether a mistaken consecration takes effect, using the case of מעשר בהמה. The debate continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The travelers' vows: everyone becomes a נזיר even though some must be wrong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה where several people make נזיר vows about who a stranger is. בית שמאי says all of them are נזירים. The גמרא then challenges: this is a mistaken consecration, yet it still takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man was coming toward a group. One said: 'I am a נזיר if this is so-and-so.' Another said: 'I am a נזיר if this is not so-and-so.' Others said: 'I am a נזיר if one of you is a נזיר,' 'if neither of you is a נזיר,' 'if both of you are נזירים,' 'if all of you are נזירים.' בית שמאי says: they are all נזירים. But this is a mistaken consecration, and still the משנה says they are all נזירים!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה it brought as proof. Then it uses that משנה to challenge the earlier explanation of רב פפא, which assumed בית שמאי does not count a mistaken consecration.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two vows contradict each other, so at least one of those speakers must be wrong. Even so, בית שמאי says every speaker is a נזיר. This shows בית שמאי holds that הקדש בטעות is still הקדש, so why did רב פפא need a different reason for the black-ox משנה?

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר; the standard wording for taking on נזירות
A consecration (or vow) made by mistake
And yet it teaches; introduces what the משנה says, used to sharpen a challenge

steps.confusionAlert: This משנה about the travelers is not the main משנה of our daf. The גמרא is quoting it from later on, only to prove what בית שמאי holds.

phrases.english: And one person was coming toward them,
and one said: 'I am a nazir if this is so-and-so,'

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד אָמַר: ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר שֶׁאֵין זֶה פְּלוֹנִי״,
phrases.english: and one said: 'I am a nazir if this is not so-and-so,'
'I am a nazir if one of you is a nazir,'
'if neither one of you is a nazir,'
phrases.notes: Each of these lines is a new person speaking, and each starts with 'I am a nazir.'

phrases.english: 'if both of you are nazirs,'
'if all of you are nazirs' —
Beit Shammai say: they are all nazirs.
But here it is a mistaken consecration,
and yet it teaches: they are all nazirs!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא הָכָא הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת הוּא, וְקָתָנֵי: כּוּלָּם נְזִירִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge to רב פפא that began just before this passage.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation, which assumes בית שמאי's ruling on the black ox is not based on הקדש בטעות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The travelers' משנה shows בית שמאי clearly holds that a mistaken vow takes effect, so the simple reason should work for the black ox too.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows clearly that בית שמאי holds הקדש בטעות is הקדש, a key idea for this whole perek.

steps.title: בית שמאי does hold mistaken consecration counts, but not as the reason here
steps.stepSummary: The answer: yes, בית שמאי holds that a mistaken consecration is a valid consecration. But the black-ox משנה is not based on that rule, so רב פפא's explanation still stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: בית שמאי holds that a mistaken consecration is a consecration. But here, in the black-ox case, that is not the reason.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits the challenge is correct about בית שמאי's general view. It explains that the black-ox משנה simply has a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the travelers is accepted: בית שמאי does hold הקדש בטעות is הקדש. But that does not force us to use this rule for the black ox. רב פפא's own reason can still explain that משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: They hold; they are of the opinion
Here, no; this case is not based on that rule

phrases.english: They say: Beit Shammai hold
that a mistaken consecration is a consecration,
but here, no.
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the black-ox משנה from earlier, where רב פפא's reason still holds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: סָבְרִי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הֶקְדֵּשׁ בְּטָעוּת הָוֵי הֶקְדֵּשׁ, הָכָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by accepting its premise but limiting it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the general rule, but says the specific משנה rests on a different reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since בית שמאי holds הקדש בטעות is הקדש, the black-ox ruling must be based on it.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית שמאי holds the rule in general, but the black-ox ruling is explained the way רב פפא said.
steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי holds הקדש בטעות is הקדש, yet a particular case can still be explained by a different reason.

steps.title: אביי: the man spoke at noon about an ox that had already gone out
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains the black-ox משנה in a new way. The man is not speaking in the morning about the future. He is speaking at noon about the past, and he got the facts wrong. So it is a true mistaken consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Don't think he was standing in the morning. Rather, what case are we dealing with? He was standing at noon and said: 'The black ox that went out of my house first shall be consecrated.' People told him: 'A white one went out.' He said to them: 'Had I known a white one went out, I would not have said black.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a different explanation of the black-ox משנה. He describes a case where the man truly made a mistake about the facts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man spoke in the morning about the future, it is not clear he made any error. אביי moves the case to noon, after the oxen already left, so the man described the past wrongly. Now it is a clear case of הקדש בטעות, and בית שמאי's ruling fits their general view.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't let it enter your mind; don't think that
What case are we dealing with here? Introduces a specific setting for a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the black ox is not הקדש. He is setting up the case so that the man clearly made a mistake, which is exactly when בית שמאי says the consecration still works.

phrases.aramaic: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לָא קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ
phrases.english: Abaye said: Do not think
that he was standing in the morning,
phrases.notes: In the morning, before the oxen left, he would be talking about the future.

phrases.english: rather, with what are we dealing here?
With one who was standing at noon, and said:
'The black ox that went out of my house first
shall be consecrated.'
And they said to him: 'A white one went out.'
And he said to them:
'Had I known that a white one went out,
I would not have said black.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: לָא קָא סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ דְּקָאֵים בְּצַפְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation of the black-ox משנה from the one kept in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The black-ox משנה is a case of a past-tense statement at noon with a factual error, so it is a true הקדש בטעות, and בית שמאי says it is הקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the black-ox ruling directly to בית שמאי's general rule of הקדש בטעות.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה uses future tense, 'a dinar that will come up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how אביי can say the case is at noon about the past. The same משנה speaks of 'a gold dinar that will come up,' which is future tense.
steps.simpleTranslation: Can you really say it deals with one standing at noon? But it teaches: 'A gold dinar that will come up'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי using the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The black-ox משנה continues with other examples, like a gold coin, written in future tense. That sounds like the speaker is talking before the event, not at noon after it, so אביי's setting seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Can you really say? Opens a challenge
That will come up; future tense

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּקָאֵים בְּטִיהֲרָא עָסֵיק?
phrases.english: But can you say it deals with one standing at noon?
But it teaches: 'A gold dinar that will come up'!
phrases.notes: This means the first coin that comes up in his hand. The point is the word 'will,' which sounds like the future.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי מָצֵית אָמְרַתְּ דְּקָאֵים בְּטִיהֲרָא עָסֵיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks אביי's setting from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the משנה is about a past event spoken at noon.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's future-tense wording ('will come up') shows the speaker is talking before the event.

steps.title: Answer: read it as 'that came up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by changing the wording to past tense: 'that came up.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'that came up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the משנה in past tense, so it fits אביי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By changing one word from future to past, the coin example also describes something that already happened. Then the whole משנה matches אביי's setting at noon.

phrases.english: Teach: 'that came up.'
phrases.notes: The גמרא is adjusting the wording here, so read it in past tense.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording of the משנה from future to past tense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's future tense proves the speaker talks before the event.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it in past tense, and the case fits אביי.

steps.title: Second challenge: 'a barrel of wine that will come up'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another future-tense example from the same משנה: a barrel of wine that will come up.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it says: 'A barrel of wine that will come up'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the same kind of challenge with another example from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This example is also written in future tense. It pushes again against אביי's past-tense setting.

keyTerms.meaning: That will come up; future tense

phrases.english: 'A barrel of wine that will come up'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge as step 4, using another example.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's past-tense setting of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another future-tense phrase in the משנה suggests the speaker is talking before the event.

steps.title: Answer: read it as 'that came up'
steps.stepSummary: Again the גמרא reads the wording in past tense: 'that came up.' This keeps אביי's explanation standing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Teach it as: 'that came up.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before, reading this example in past tense too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With both examples read in past tense, the whole משנה fits a man speaking at noon about events that already happened. אביי's explanation survives.

keyTerms.meaning: That came up (feminine, for the barrel); past tense

steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי, the black-ox משנה is a past-tense statement with a factual mistake, a true case of הקדש בטעות. The משנה's future-tense words are read in past tense to fit.

phrases.english: Teach: 'that came up.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 6 the same way step 5 answered step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the wording from future to past tense.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The future tense shows the speaker is talking before the event.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read it in past tense; the whole משנה fits אביי's setting at noon.

steps.title: רב חסדא: white oxen are the better kind
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says a black ox among white ones is flawed, and a white patch on a black ox is a flaw.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: A black ox among white ones is flawed, and white on a black ox is flawed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new statement from רב חסדא about which ox color is better. This sets up a challenge from the black-ox משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא is telling us that white is the better color for oxen. A black ox stands out as weaker next to white ones. White spots on a black ox count as a defect.

keyTerms.meaning: A black one (here, a black ox)
A white one (here, a white ox or white patch)
Is flawed, is weaker or of lower quality

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of this section tests רב חסדא's view against the black-ox case in the משנה.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
A black one among white ones is flawed,
a white one on a black one is flawed.
phrases.notes: He means a white patch on a black ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic that connects to the black-ox case of the same משנה discussed in Steps 3-7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For oxen, white is the better color. Black among white is weak, and white on black is a defect.

steps.title: The black-ox case seems to show white is worse
steps.stepSummary: If people consecrate the worse item, then בית שמאי calling the white ox consecrated means white is worse, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: 'The black ox that comes out of my house first is consecrated,' and a white one came out. We assumed that a person consecrates with a stingy eye. Yet בית שמאי say the white one is consecrated. So the white one must be the worse animal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא from the black-ox case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא assumes that a person giving to הקדש means to give the worse item. בית שמאי say the white ox becomes consecrated even though he said 'black'. That only makes sense if white is worse, which is the opposite of what רב חסדא said.

keyTerms.meaning: We were thinking, we first assumed
With a stingy eye: giving the lesser item

phrases.english: We learned:
"The black one that will come out of my house first is consecrated."
phrases.notes: The case in the משנה is that a white one came out instead.

phrases.english: It entered our minds:
when a person consecrates, he consecrates with a stingy eye,
and Beit Shammai say it is consecrated!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: שָׁחוֹר שֶׁיֵּצֵא מִבֵּיתִי רִאשׁוֹן הֶקְדֵּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב חסדא's statement from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that white oxen are better.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person consecrates the worse item. בית שמאי consecrate the white ox, so white must be worse.

steps.title: Testing the idea that people consecrate generously
steps.stepSummary: Maybe people consecrate the better item? No. In the gold-dinar case, בית שמאי say the silver coin that came up is consecrated.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what, does a person consecrate with a generous eye? Look at the next case: 'The gold dinar that comes up in my hand first,' and a silver one came up, and בית שמאי say it is consecrated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the opposite idea, that people consecrate generously, which would save רב חסדא. It knocks that idea down from the gold-dinar case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If people gave the better item, a silver coin should not become consecrated when he said gold. But בית שמאי say it is consecrated. So the 'generous eye' idea does not fit the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather, what? (testing the other option)
With a generous eye: giving the better item

phrases.english: But rather, what?
He consecrates with a generous eye?
"The gold dinar that will come up in my hand first,"
and a silver one came up,
Beit Shammai say: consecrated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the opposite of Step 9's assumption and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that people consecrate generously.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Silver is worse than gold, yet בית שמאי make it consecrated. That fits the stingy view, not the generous one.

steps.title: Problem for the stingy view: oil is better than wine
steps.stepSummary: If people consecrate stingily, why is the oil consecrated when he said wine? Oil is worth more.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what, does he consecrate with a stingy eye? Look: 'A barrel of wine that comes up in my hand first,' and one of oil came up, and בית שמאי say it is consecrated. But oil is better than wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now challenges the stingy-eye idea from the wine-and-oil case in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person means to give the worse item, the oil should not become consecrated, because oil is worth more than wine. Yet בית שמאי say it is consecrated. So the stingy view also seems to break down.

phrases.english: But rather, what? He consecrates with a stingy eye?

phrases.aramaic: חָבִית שֶׁל יַיִן שֶׁתַּעֲלֶה בְּיָדִי רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: A barrel of wine that will come up in my hand first,
and one of oil came up,
Beit Shammai say: consecrated.
But oil is better than wine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the stingy view from Step 9 and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that people consecrate stingily.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Oil is worth more than wine, yet the oil becomes consecrated. That fits a generous giver, not a stingy one.

steps.title: In the Galilee, wine is worth more than oil
steps.stepSummary: The משנה was taught in the גליל, where wine is worth more than oil, so the stingy view still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is the problem, it is not difficult. The משנה was taught in the גליל, where wine is worth more than oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wine-and-oil problem by saying where the משנה was taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the גליל, oil was cheaper than wine. So the oil was the worse item there, and making it consecrated fits the stingy view. Now every case in the משנה fits 'people consecrate stingily'.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no problem

steps.whyThisMatters: With the stingy view secure, the black-ox case goes back to being a problem for רב חסדא.

phrases.english: If it is because of this, it is not difficult:
They taught it in the Galilee,
where wine is better than oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Local circumstances: the value of items depends on the place where the משנה was taught.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Oil is always worth more than wine, so consecrating oil shows generosity.
steps.terutzMaskana: In the גליל wine is worth more, so the oil was the lesser item, and the stingy view stands.

steps.title: The black-ox case is still hard for רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: Since people consecrate stingily, the first case (the black ox) still shows white is worse, against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first case of the משנה is difficult for רב חסדא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back its challenge to רב חסדא now that the stingy view is firm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case in the משנה fits the idea that a person gives the lesser item. So in the first case, the white ox that became consecrated must be the lesser ox. That goes against רב חסדא's claim that white is better.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of the משנה

phrases.english: The first part is difficult for Rav Chisda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that Step 12 has secured the stingy view, it restates the challenge of Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that white oxen are better.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: People consecrate the lesser item. The white ox was consecrated, so white is the lesser color.

steps.title: רב חסדא meant only קרמנאי oxen
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that he only said white is better for the קרמנאי breed of ox.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא can tell you: When I said white is better, I was talking about a קרמנאי ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רב חסדא by limiting his statement to one breed of ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a קרמנאי ox, white is the better color. For regular oxen, black is better. The משנה is about regular oxen, so white is the lesser one there, and there is no clash.

keyTerms.meaning: He can say to you (an answer given on someone's behalf)
A קרמנאי ox, a breed where white is better

steps.whatToRemember: People consecrate 'with a stingy eye,' giving the lesser item. Every case in the משנה fits this, wine and oil included, since in the גליל wine was worth more. רב חסדא's 'white is better' applies only to קרמנאי oxen. For regular oxen, black is better.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda can say to you:
When I said it, it was about a Karmanian ox.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the statement to a specific case (one breed of ox).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב חסדא meant that white is better for all oxen.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only קרמנאי oxen. For regular oxen, as in the משנה, black is better.

steps.title: רב חסדא: what each ox color is good for
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא teaches that a black ox is best for its hide, a red ox for its meat, and a white ox for plowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב חסדא said: a black ox is good for its hide, a red ox is good for its meat, and a white ox is good for plowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another statement of רב חסדא about oxen colors. This sets up a new question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here each color has its own strength, and white is best for plowing. That suggests white is not simply better or worse overall. It depends on what you need the ox for.

phrases.english: And Rav Chisda said:
A black one is good for its hide,
a red one is good for its meat,
a white one is good for plowing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second statement of רב חסדא about oxen colors, after step 14 explained his first statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each ox color has its own best use: black for hide, red for meat, white for plowing.

steps.title: But רב חסדא said a black ox among white ones is inferior
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges this with רב חסדא's other statement, which says a black ox among white ones is deficient.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב חסדא say that a black ox among white ones is deficient?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב חסדא seems to contradict himself. One statement gives each color its own value, and the other calls black flatly weaker than white.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Black among white is deficient' sounds like black is worse in every way. But in step 15 black was the best color for hide. So which is it?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (opens a contradiction)
A black one among white ones

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Chisda say:
A black one among white ones is deficient!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 15 with another statement of the same אמורא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's statement that each color has its own advantage (step 15).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His other statement calls black weaker than white with no limits, which clashes with black being the best color for hide.

steps.title: That was only about the קרמונאי breed
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא answers that 'black among white is deficient' was said only about oxen of the קרמונאי breed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I said that, I meant only the ox of the קרמונאי breed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by limiting the second statement to one breed of ox.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ordinary oxen, each color has its own use, as in step 15. Only for the קרמונאי breed is black weaker than white. This matches the answer already given in step 14.

keyTerms.meaning: The קרמונאי breed (a specific type of ox)

steps.whatToRemember: Both of רב חסדא's statements stand. The general rule is that each color has its own use. 'Black is weaker' applies only to the קרמונאי breed.

phrases.english: When I said it, it was about the Karmanian ox.
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is talking about himself here. It's the same answer the גמרא gave just before, in step 14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting one statement to a specific case (one breed)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Black among white is deficient' applies to all oxen, so it clashes with step 15.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies only to the קרמונאי breed. For other oxen, each color has its own use.

steps.title: משנה: a נזיר who asks a חכם about his vow
steps.stepSummary: New משנה: if the חכם holds him to the vow, he counts from the day he vowed. If the חכם dissolves the vow, the animal he set aside goes back to graze with the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who vowed to be a נזיר and asked a חכם about it, and the חכם held him bound, counts from the time he vowed. If he asked a חכם and the חכם dissolved the vow, and he had an animal set aside for his offering, it goes out and grazes with the flock.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with two outcomes of asking a חכם about a נזירות vow. The second outcome will become the base for the debate that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vow stands, the days he already lived since vowing count toward his נזירות. If the vow is dissolved, it is as if there never was a vow. So the animal he set aside was never really holy, and it simply returns to the flock.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
Asked a sage (to dissolve the vow)
And he held him bound (did not dissolve the vow)
An animal set aside (for his נזיר offering)
It grazes with the flock (it goes back to being ordinary)

steps.confusionAlert: 'וַאֲסָרוֹ' does not mean the חכם made something new forbidden. It means the חכם found no reason to dissolve the vow, so the person stays bound.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
One who vowed to be a nazir,
and asked a sage, and he held him bound —
phrases.notes: He asked the sage to undo the vow, but the sage found no grounds and left it in place.

phrases.english: counts from the time that he vowed.
If he asked a sage and he dissolved it,
and he had an animal set aside —
it shall go out and graze among the flock.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא's discussion of the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the vow is upheld, he counts from when he vowed. If it is dissolved, the animal set aside is not holy and returns to the flock.

steps.title: בית הלל: you agree a mistaken consecration is not holy here
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל argue to בית שמאי that this case is a הקדש טעות, and even בית שמאי agree the animal goes back to the flock.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to בית שמאי: Don't you agree in this case, which is a consecration made by mistake, that the animal goes out and grazes with the flock?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל use the משנה's case to attack בית שמאי's view from the previous משנה, that הקדש טעות is still holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man set aside the animal believing he was a נזיר, and that turned out to be a mistake once the vow was dissolved. If בית שמאי agree the animal is not holy here, then a mistaken consecration does not take effect, against their own view.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't you agree? (a challenge built on what the other side accepts)

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to Beit Shammai:
Don't you agree in this case
that it is a mistaken consecration,
that it goes out and grazes among the flock?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ruling of step 18 to reopen the earlier debate about הקדש טעות.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's view that הקדש טעות is holy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Here the consecration rested on a mistake, yet everyone agrees the animal is not holy. So a mistaken consecration does not take effect.

steps.title: בית שמאי: the animal tithe case where a mistaken 'tenth' is holy
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer with מעשר בהמה: if someone mistakenly calls the ninth, tenth, or eleventh animal by the wrong number, it becomes holy.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי said to them: Don't you agree that one who mistakenly called the ninth 'tenth,' the tenth 'ninth,' and the eleventh 'tenth' makes each of them holy?
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי push back with a case that בית הלל also accept, where a mistake does create holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מעשר בהמה, the animals pass by one at a time and the tenth becomes holy. If he wrongly calls the ninth or eleventh 'tenth,' it still becomes holy. בית שמאי say this proves a mistaken consecration does take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: The tithe of animals (every tenth animal becomes holy)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai said to them:
Don't you agree about one who erred
and called the ninth 'tenth,'
phrases.notes: This is about מעשר בהמה, where the animals are counted one by one and the tenth becomes holy.

phrases.english: and the tenth 'ninth,'
and the eleventh 'tenth,'
that it is consecrated?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אִי אַתֶּם מוֹדִים בְּמִי שֶׁטָּעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: בית שמאי answer בית הלל's challenge with a counter-case.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's view that הקדש טעות is not holy.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In מעשר בהמה, a mistaken call of 'tenth' makes the animal holy, and בית הלל agree. So mistakes can create holiness.

steps.title: בית הלל: the rod alone does not make it holy
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer that the tithing rod and the mistaken word do not make the animal holy, since a mistake on the eighth or twelfth animal does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל said to them: It is not the rod that makes it holy. What if he mistakenly placed the rod on the eighth or the twelfth animal? Did he do anything?
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל reject בית שמאי's proof. They show that a mistake in tithing does not always create holiness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If mistakes made animals holy, then calling the eighth or twelfth 'tenth' would also work. It does not. So the ninth and eleventh must become holy for some special reason, not because a mistake takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: Rod (used to mark the tithe animals)

phrases.english: Beit Hillel said to them:
It is not the rod that consecrated it.
phrases.notes: When tithing, he touches each tenth animal with a rod. בית הלל say the touch and the mistaken call are not what make it holy.

phrases.english: And what if he erred
and placed the rod
on the eighth or on the twelfth,
did he perhaps do anything?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל לֹא הַשֵּׁבֶט קִידְּשׁוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects בית שמאי's proof from מעשר בהמה in step 20.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from מעשר בהמה that mistakes create holiness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A mistake on the eighth or twelfth animal does nothing. So the tithe case is not built on 'a mistake takes effect.'

steps.title: The verse that makes the tenth holy also makes the ninth holy
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל explain that the ninth (and eleventh) become holy only because the same פסוק that makes the tenth holy includes them too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the פסוק that made the tenth holy also made the ninth holy.
steps.whatsHappening: בית הלל give the real reason the mistaken ninth becomes holy: a special rule from the פסוק, not a general rule about mistakes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holiness of the ninth comes straight from the פסוק, which is a special rule for מעשר בהמה only. So it proves nothing about הקדש טעות in general, and בית הלל's view stands.
steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל hold that הקדש טעות is not holy. The mistaken ninth or eleventh in מעשר בהמה is holy only because of a special פסוק, not because mistakes take effect.

phrases.english: Rather, the verse that consecrated the tenth —
it consecrated the ninth

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection in step 21 by giving the real source for the ninth becoming holy.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The source is a special פסוק, not a general rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ninth becomes holy because a mistaken consecration takes effect.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ninth becomes holy only because the פסוק of מעשר בהמה includes it, so the case cannot be used for הקדש טעות in general.
